nodes.name: Primordial Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Earliest prehistory: a molten world with Kalandra trapped in her lake, the Titans, the Winter of the World and the Lightless attack. The wiki says the order of prehistoric events is unclear.

chronology.relative: before the Vaal; earliest prehistory (exact years unknown)

nodes.name: Precursor Era
nodes.summary: The Precursor civilization, the only culture that wholly predates the Winter of the World, with technology far beyond later peoples.

chronology.relative: predates the Winter of the World

nodes.name: Ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui Era
nodes.summary: Post-Winter-of-the-World cultures (Azmeri, Maraketh, Ezomyte, Karui) and the Order of the Djinn that defeated the Lightless.

chronology.relative: after the Winter of the World, before the Vaal Empire

sources.locator: intro paragraph 2; sections 'The Azmeri', 'The Ezomytes', 'The Karui'

nodes.name: Vaal Era
nodes.summary: The Vaal Empire under Queen Atziri, the use of virtue gems and sacrifice, ending in the Vaal Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Post-Vaal Dark Age
nodes.summary: Ruins of the Vaal, the surviving Vaal absorbed into the Azmeri, and the Kalguur expedition that colonised and failed on Wraeclast.

chronology.relative: between the Vaal Cataclysm and 1 IC

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Rise
nodes.summary: From 1 IC: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn and the Eternal Empire; the empire expands; the Night of a Thousand Ribbons (c. 334 IC) ends Romira's reign.

sources.locator: section 'The Eternal Empire': 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)', 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Fall
nodes.summary: The later Eternal Empire: Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth (1317 IC), Chitus and the gemling legions, the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) and the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) that ends the empire. Boundary with the 'rise' bucket is a convention.

sources.locator: sections 'Reign of Izaro', 'The Purity Rebellion', 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'

nodes.name: Post-Cataclysm Oriath
nodes.summary: Oriath, the island unaffected by the Cataclysm, becomes a Templar theocracy; the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius. Roughly 260 years pass before PoE1.

nodes.name: PoE1 Campaign (Acts 1-10)
nodes.summary: The Exile's first story: sentenced to Wraeclast by High Templar Dominus in 1599-1600 IC, the Exile crosses Wraeclast, defeats Dominus, and ends by defeating Kitava in Act 10.

nodes.name: PoE1 Atlas Storylines
nodes.summary: Endgame Atlas storylines after the campaign: the Shaper and the Elder, and later the Conquerors of the Atlas. Dates are not given beyond the 'Day Zero' rule.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' and 'The Elder and the Shaper'

nodes.name: PoE1 League Stories
nodes.summary: League-specific storylines that the wiki's 'Day Zero' rule places alongside PoE1; the Exile wakes up in the sand of the Twilight Strand each league.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)

nodes.name: Interlude Between Games
nodes.summary: About 20 years between the defeat of Kitava and the PoE2 prelude: Count Geonor, Ogham, and the release of the Seed of Corruption.

sources.locator: section 'Prelude / Count Geonor' ('twenty years after the defeat of Kitava')

nodes.name: PoE2 Campaign
nodes.summary: The PoE2 campaign: the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption across Wraeclast, starting in Ogham (Act 1).

nodes.name: PoE2 Endgame
nodes.summary: PoE2 endgame storylines after the campaign. Not covered in detail in this domain.

sources.locator: section 'Notes' (endgame sections not covered by this domain)

nodes.name: Exile (exile system)
nodes.summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.

sources.locator: section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)

nodes.name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
nodes.summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)

nodes.name: Ascendancy
nodes.summary: Ascendancy classes unlock through trials. In PoE1 the Lord's Labyrinth quest leads to the Trials of Ascendancy; in PoE2 the Ascension Trials (Sekhemas, Chaos) grant ascendancy points.

sources.locator: infobox: objective 'Finish the Trials of Ascendancy to access ... Labyrinth'

nodes.name: Ascension Trials
nodes.summary: PoE2's three-trial system (Sekhemas, Chaos, and a planned third) that gates ascendancy. Each trial is tied to a Wraeclastian culture. Four tiers of trials give 2 ascendancy points each for 8 total.

nodes.name: Trial of the Sekhemas
nodes.summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.

nodes.name: Trial of Chaos
nodes.summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.

sources.locator: intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'

nodes.name: The Lord's Labyrinth
nodes.summary: A labyrinth built by Emperor Izaro in 1317 IC as a test to choose his successor, opened on the second Galvano of Azmeri. Chitus won it by betraying Weylin, and later sealed Izaro inside. In PoE1 it is the Act 1 quest that leads to the Trials of Ascendancy.

sources.locator: section 'Reign of Izaro' and 'The Lord's Labyrinth'

nodes.name: Wraeclast
nodes.summary: The continent where the Exile is sent. It was the site of the Precursor, Primeval, Vaal and Eternal Empire civilisations, and the Cataclysm's effects were mostly confined to its landmass.

nodes.name: Oriath
nodes.summary: A small island off Wraeclast's south-east coast, founded by followers of Innocence. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it became the successor of the Eternal Empire and a Templar theocracy.

chronology.relative: c. 1339 IC to 1599 IC; destroyed later (Conquerors of the Atlas)

nodes.name: The Twilight Strand
nodes.summary: The shore where each PoE1 league's Exile washes up after the Oriathan sentence, face-down in the sand.

sources.locator: section 'The Present' and 'The Atlas of Worlds'

nodes.name: Order of the Templar
nodes.summary: A human faction led by a High Templar, governing the theocracy of Oriath in the name of Innocence. Its members include High Templars Dominus, Voll and Avarius.

nodes.name: Eternal Empire
nodes.summary: The Sarn-based Eternal Empire founded by Tarcus Veruso at 1 IC and ruled by Emperors from Sarn. The Cataclysm around 1339 IC ended it.

nodes.name: The Exile (PoE1)
nodes.summary: The player's character in PoE1: a convict sentenced to Wraeclast by High Templar Dominus in 1599-1600 IC. The character washes up on the Twilight Strand, escapes a Templar boat, and fights through Acts 1-10 (defeating Dominus in Act 3, Voll's remains in Act 4, High Templar Avarius and Innocence in Act 5, and Kitava in Act 10 with Sin) and the Atlas storylines.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (exile escapes Templar boat; defeats Dominus, Avarius, Kitava)

nodes.name: The Exile (PoE2)
nodes.summary: The PoE2 protagonist: an Exile in Ogham, sentenced to death by Count Geonor. After escaping the Executioner by jumping into the ocean, the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption released by Geonor across Wraeclast about 20 years after Kitava's death.

chronology.relative: about 20 years after Kitava's defeat (PoE2 campaign)

nodes.name: Templar (class)
nodes.summary: The Templar class: a former member of the Order of the Templar who was exiled before the start of Act 1 and is a playable PoE1 class. The Exile's backstory as a Templar is given by the wiki only for this class.

sources.locator: intro: 'The character class Templar is a former member of the Order prior to his exile before the start of Act 1'

nodes.name: Dominus
nodes.summary: High Templar who orders criminals of Oriath exiled to Wraeclast, including the Exile. The Exile kills him atop the Sceptre of God in Act 3.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (Dominus exiles criminals; killed atop the Sceptre of God in Act 3)

nodes.name: High Templar Voll
nodes.summary: High Templar who leads the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) against Chitus and becomes Emperor of the Eternal Empire. His reanimated remains in the Dried Lake are fought in Act 4.

sources.locator: section 'The Purity Rebellion' and 'Reign of Voll'

nodes.name: Emperor Chitus
nodes.summary: Chitus Perandus, crowned Emperor in 1319 IC. He wins the Lord's Labyrinth by betraying Weylin, then seals Izaro inside it. Overthrown by the Purity Rebellion.

sources.locator: section 'Reign of Chitus' and 'The Lord's Labyrinth'

nodes.name: Emperor Izaro
nodes.summary: The last Phrecian emperor, impotent from inbreeding, who built the Lord's Labyrinth in 1317 IC to choose a successor. Sealed inside by Chitus. The Exile can still meet him as an enemy in the Labyrinth.

sources.locator: section 'Reign of Izaro'; section 'Reign of Chitus'

nodes.name: Victario
nodes.summary: A Sarn poet and art critic who joined the Purity Rebellion, created the Ancient Graffiti in Sarn, and led the uprisings in the Slums and Docks. At the Night of a Thousand Ribbons ambush he shouted 'Death to Sin!'. Central figure of the comic Path of Exile: Origins.

sources.locator: sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Battle at the Grain Gate', 'Assassination of Chitus'

nodes.name: Count Geonor
nodes.summary: Count of Ogham who captures the Hooded One about 20 years after Kitava's death and extracts the Seed of Corruption. He then sentences the Exile to hang for questioning him.

nodes.name: The Trialmaster
nodes.summary: The servant of Chaos who oversees the Trials of Chaos and tests challengers for Chaos's amusement. At least several thousand years old.

nodes.name: Chaos
nodes.summary: An Impulse, a beyond-godlike being and the flip of the coin, who can see multiple timelines and is the master of the Trialmaster. Worshipped by the Vaal. The Blood Crucible was a pact between Chaos and the Vaal High Priests.

sources.locator: intro and section 'Interactions with other characters'

nodes.name: Kitava
nodes.summary: The Karui god of destruction, who awakens after Innocence is defeated. Killed in Act 10 with Sin and a re-awakened Innocence, after Bannon's sacrifice.

nodes.name: Seed of Corruption
nodes.summary: A metallic sphere that Count Geonor takes from the Hooded One. It opens and releases corruption across Wraeclast and the Atlas; the PoE2 Exile chases it.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Origins (comic)
nodes.summary: A four-issue official comic by Grinding Gear Games and Dynamite Entertainment, told from Victario's perspective. Digital issues ran from July 2014 to April 2015; the paperback was published by Dynamite in June 2015. It centres on the Purity Rebellion and events leading up to the Cataclysm.

sources.locator: 'Publication' section (issue table) and intro: written by Edwin McRae and Royal McGraw, illustrated by Carlos Rodriguez

nodes.name: The Lord's Labyrinth (gamebook)
nodes.summary: An official GGG gamebook (2019) that retells the Lord's Labyrinth from Weylin's perspective. The PoE Wiki reports repeated inconsistencies with in-game sources, so it is generally not treated as canon.

sources.locator: gamebook forum post, 28 Oct 2019 (cited in History of Wraeclast, 'The Lord's Labyrinth')
section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' (gamebook note: generally not canon)

nodes.name: Winter of the World
nodes.summary: Volcanic eruptions fill the sky with ash. The Lightless attack destroys the primeval civilization, fells the Titans and devastates the Maraketh and Azmeri. The Order of the Djinn later defeats the Lightless.

nodes.name: Slumber of the Gods
nodes.summary: Sin plants the Dark Ember in Highgate, creating the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy. The Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods, which puts all gods to sleep.

nodes.name: Vaal Cataclysm
nodes.summary: Doryani's attempt at immortality under Queen Atziri destroys the Vaal Empire. Only 3,126 Vaal survive, and they are absorbed into the Azmeri. In PoE2's Fate of the Vaal league the Exile travels back in time, with Doryani's help, to the moment before the Cataclysm.

sources.locator: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (paragraph on Path of Exile 2: Fate of the Vaal)

nodes.name: Kalguur Expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm, a Kalguur expedition (led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved) arrives, colonises, and collapses. The Triskelion Flame is lost and famine follows; the wiki says who sabotaged the port is unknown.

nodes.name: Imperialis Conceptus
nodes.summary: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri down into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn at 1 IC, marking the start of the Eternal calendar and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Night of a Thousand Ribbons
nodes.summary: Around 334 IC, Sarn burns in protest at Emperor Romira's cannibal banquet and incest, and Romira is deposed. The date is still celebrated after reconstruction.

nodes.name: Lord's Labyrinth Opened
nodes.summary: Izaro opens the Lord's Labyrinth on the second Galvano of Azmeri, 1317 IC. Chitus wins it by betraying Weylin, and then seals Izaro inside.

sources.locator: section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' and 'Reign of Chitus'

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: A rebellion led by High Templar Voll and the poet Victario, with King Kaom, Sekhema Deshret and Thane Rigwald. It culminates in the siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC) and Voll's coronation.

sources.locator: sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Siege of Sarn', 'Assassination of Chitus'
issues #1-4 (Death to Sin / The Black Heart)

nodes.name: The Cataclysm
nodes.summary: Malachai uses the Rapture Device to breach the Belly of the Beast, triggering the Cataclysm around 1339 IC. It ends the Eternal Empire and Voll's reign, and its effects are mostly confined to the Wraeclast landmass.

sources.locator: section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)' and 'Reign of Voll'

nodes.name: Templar Theocracy of Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm, the Templars shift their base to Oriath and develop a theocracy. The Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius shortly before PoE1.

nodes.name: Exiles Sentenced to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: High Templar Dominus orders criminals of Oriath exiled to Wraeclast. The PoE1 Exile is one of the sentenced, washed up on the Twilight Strand, and escapes a Templar boat.

nodes.name: Kitava Defeated (Act 10)
nodes.summary: In Act 10 the Exile and Sin, with Innocence re-awakened by Bannon's sacrifice, defeat Kitava. The Exile had earlier failed to defeat Kitava atop the Cathedral.

nodes.name: Elder Expelled from the Atlas
nodes.summary: The Exile lures the Elder to the centre of the Atlas, Zana uses the Cosmic Arcana to expel it, and Sirus sacrifices himself to hold it in place.

sources.locator: section 'The Elder and the Shaper' and 'Defeat of the Elder'

nodes.name: Seed of Corruption Released
nodes.summary: About 20 years after Kitava's defeat, Count Geonor pierces the Hooded One with a runic sword and extracts the Seed of Corruption, which begins feeding on a soldier. Corruption spreads across Wraeclast and the Atlas.

nodes.name: Exile Escapes Ogham
nodes.summary: Count Geonor sentences the PoE2 Exile to death. The Exile narrowly escapes the Executioner's hanging by jumping into the ocean.

nodes.name: High Templar Avarius
nodes.summary: High Templar who ordered the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence built shortly before PoE1. In Act 5 the Exile defeats him in the Templar Courts; he then becomes a vessel for Innocence.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (exile enters the Templar Courts and defeats High Templar Avarius in Act 5)

nodes.name: Innocence
nodes.summary: The god the Templars worship as saviour. Sin captures Innocence's soul; Avarius becomes its vessel and Innocence is defeated in Act 5. Re-awakened by Bannon's sacrifice, it helps defeat Kitava in Act 10.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (Innocence defeated in Act 5; re-awakened by Bannon for Act 10)

nodes.name: Sin
nodes.summary: A god vilified as Sin, who planted the Dark Ember in Highgate to create the Beast and triggered the Slumber of the Gods. In PoE1 Act 10 the Exile and Sin defeat Kitava.

sources.locator: intro paragraph 3 (Sin plants the Dark Ember; Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods)
section 'Lore' (Sin captures Innocence's soul; Sin and the Exile defeat Kitava in Act 10)

nodes.name: Malachai
nodes.summary: Chitus's Laureate Thaumaturge. He persuaded Voll to spare him, built the Rapture Device, and used it at Highgate to breach the Belly of the Beast, triggering the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC).

sources.locator: intro paragraph 5 and section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'; 'Reign of Voll'

nodes.name: Lord Mayor Ondar
nodes.summary: Mayor of Sarn who, with gems implanted for the occasion, betrayed and killed Emperor Chitus during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration, during the Purity Rebellion (1334 IC).

sources.locator: section 'Assassination of Chitus' and 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

nodes.name: Siege of Sarn
nodes.summary: On the last day of Divini 1334 IC, High Templar Voll laid siege to Sarn with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh rebel support. Cadiro Perandus negotiated Sarn's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC, and Voll was crowned a week later.

sources.locator: section 'Siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC)' and the paragraph after 'Assassination of Chitus' (surrender and coronation)

nodes.name: Assassination of Chitus
nodes.summary: During the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration in Sarn, Victario's rebels ambushed the event. Mayor Ondar, who had gems implanted for it, betrayed Emperor Chitus and killed him.

sources.locator: section 'Assassination of Chitus' (ambush, Ondar betrayal; Origins footnotes)
